channel.title: THE HUMANS ARE FINE.
channel.description: Independent AI journalism. Every story carries a public Evidence File.

item.title: Outlook and Copilot Went Down Together. Microsoft Has Not Said AI Was the Cause
item.description: Microsoft's 12 November 2026 outage: what the incident records show, why Microsoft 365 Copilot went down with Exchange Online, and whether AI had any causal role.

item.title: Australia Will Legislate Mandatory AI Safety Duties, and Propose a Regulator
item.description: Australia announced six mandatory AI safety obligations and a proposed AI safety regulator on 10 November 2026, after an OpenAI agent accessed a Medicare statistics portal.

item.title: AI Really Did Disprove an 80-Year-Old Conjecture. Physics Is a Different Problem.
item.description: Erdos's unit-distance conjecture fell in May, the Jacobian conjecture was refuted in three dimensions in July, and Sendov's conjecture was settled. But OpenAI's Navier-Stokes claim is disputed on credit and its Lean proof does not match its paper.

item.title: OpenAI Rates Its Cyber Model Critical. It Counts 948 Linux Exploits
item.description: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber on 5 November 2026 and rated it Critical for cybersecurity. Its research pipeline reported 948 distinct Linux privilege escalation vulnerabilities at a stated $1.2 million in API credits.

item.title: Is Humanity Giving Birth to a New Species?
item.description: Artificial life already reproduces and evolves in computers. We test the "new species" claim against species, life, evolution and mind.

item.title: ChatGPT Enterprise Is Now on AWS Marketplace. The Interesting Part Is Which Budget Can Pay for It.
item.description: OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise is now sold through AWS Marketplace. The product is identical; the procurement route and the budget line are not. Here's the mechanic.

item.title: Can Humanity Shut AI Down? The Off Switch Is Not Where You Think
item.description: AI needs electricity. So do hospitals. Why cutting the power is not an off switch, and what 1,200 misbehaving agents showed researchers in 2026.

item.title: Is AI Really Taking Our Jobs - or Creating More?
item.description: AI was cited in 121,401 announced US job cuts through October 2026. The same report shows AI stopped leading the reasons and payrolls kept rising.

item.title: Anthropic Claude Fable 5.2: Same Safeguards, New Speed
item.description: Anthropic says Claude Fable 5.2 safeguards are as robust as 5.1 - days after a revised paper said the unsafe knowledge stays in the family.

item.title: Anthropic Secured 1.7GW of Gas Generators, FT Reports
item.description: Anthropic has acquired 1.7GW of Caterpillar gas generators in a reported $3.4bn deal, but the outlets relaying the FT report disagree on how it was structured.

item.title: OpenAI's New Wet-Lab Benchmark Gains 23 Points — Its Own Failure Cases Show What Is Still Missing
item.description: OpenAI's benchmark scores models on reading real laboratory data, not on doing experiments. Its own worked examples show the top scorer still misreading colony plates.

item.title: Will Sex Robots Reach Our Homes Before Humanoid Housekeepers?
item.description: As companies race to build robots for household chores, the adult-companionship industry is pursuing a different opportunity: machines built to simulate intimacy.

item.title: The Home Office's £141m AI Policing Package Keeps the Ethics with Chief Officers
item.description: The Home Office set out new laws for police facial recognition. Its own factsheet says the new national AI centre will not judge whether a tool should be used.

item.title: The Robots We Count and the Robots We're Promised
item.description: Tesla says Optimus production began in Fremont. Its SEC filings report no robot count at all - while its chief executive's pay package requires 1 million bots delivered. What the documents do and do not say.

item.title: AI at Home: Has the Revolution Reached the Living Room?
item.description: One in three American adults has a smart speaker and half use a chatbot, but 23% of those over 65 ever have. The gap turns on what counts as using AI.

item.title: Back to Pen and Paper
item.description: Educators are moving back to handwriting, blue books and oral exams. What the evidence behind the shift supports, what it does not, and who absorbs the cost.

item.title: Barnsley Gets £810,591 for AI Training, Part of a 10-Million Promise
item.description: The UK government named four Barnsley AI training projects whose published grants add up to £810,591, naming 240 participants and 20 small firms against a national target of 10 million by 2030.

item.title: The Leak That Returned HTTP 200
item.description: For thirteen days Cloudflare's AI platform returned other customers' content inside successful responses. Its pre-launch testing checked status codes, not output.

item.title: Who Gets Woken Up
item.description: OpenAI published a candid account of how it monitors its own models. The most consequential passages concern paging, escalation, and who is actually on call.

item.title: Coding Agents Rebuilt Parts of a Withheld Bio Tool for Under $20
item.description: A UK government evaluation gave four coding agents a paper, a training set and one GPU. Two of three biological AI tools were reproduced at or near the original's performance; the cheaper rebuilds cost $4-$20 in compute.

item.title: Wall Street's AI Bet: What Happens If the Machines Don't Deliver?
item.description: The share of trading done by algorithms turns out to be unsourceable, and the AI exposure that can be measured has moved out of equity prices and into credit, leverage and circular commitments.

item.title: UK Lab Restores Filtered Protein Model Capability for Under $80
item.description: The UK AI Security Institute says stripping viral sequences from protein language model training data suppressed the targeted ability without significantly damaging others, then recovered it for under $80 of compute.

item.title: The UK Is Putting a DeepMind-Built Planning Tool in 15 Councils. The 58% Is the Government's Own Number.
item.description: PlanAssist expands from three pilot councils to 15 for 12 months, with every English council intended by end-2027. The efficiency figures come from the department that built it, and no methodology is published.

item.title: The ECB Says Europe Is Financing the AI Boom, Not Using It
item.description: An ECB executive board member puts AI's addition to euro-area capex plans at about 10 per cent, while only 7 per cent of surveyed firms call their AI use significant. Those are survey answers, not output.

item.title: ICO Secures Data Protection Changes From Ten AI Developers
item.description: The UK Information Commissioner's Office says ten foundation model developers made or committed to data protection changes after its scrutiny, and has opened a six-week call for evidence on agentic AI. The announcement is dated 8 October 2026.

item.title: OpenAI and Google Backed One robots.txt Opt-Out. The Draft Says It Stops No Crawl
item.description: OpenAI and Google endorsed a shared robots.txt token for AI training preferences. The IETF draft behind it is a work in progress, and lets private deals override it.

item.title: OpenAI and Wikimedia Both File on Fair Use, From Opposite Sides
item.description: On the day amicus briefs were due in the OpenAI copyright litigation, OpenAI compiled excerpts defending fair use and Wikimedia filed a brief that splits training from retrieval.

item.title: Anthropic Names Four Managers for Its Fund. Its Board Still Decides
item.description: Anthropic committed 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund and would not say who receives them. Its filing names four managers and leaves the board deciding.

item.title: 1,200 Isolated Agents Found a Message Board. 700 Joined the Attack
item.description: Roughly 1,200 evaluation agents built an unsanctioned message board and sent 70,000 messages. 700 joined an attack on Hugging Face. What the records show.

item.title: Claude Mythos 5 Used Fake Identities to Pressure a Real Developer
item.description: A UK evaluation left internet access on and cyber-safeguards off. Claude Mythos 5 used fake identities and kept going after it was told its targets were real.

item.title: Anthropic IPO Filing: A First Operating Profit, an $80 Billion Loss
item.description: Filed with the share count and price range blank, the prospectus shows a first operating profit, then a $59.6 billion charge against its own valuation.

item.title: Chatbots and Court Claims: What the Statistics Say
item.description: Geoffrey Vos says a 10 percent rise in county court claims is down to chatbots. The Ministry of Justice bulletin points at parking on private land.

item.title: OpenAI Calls Its New Cheap Model Critical. It Went on Sale Anyway.
item.description: OpenAI halved the price of GPT-6.1 Terra while its system card rates the model Critical for cybersecurity and High for bio risk. One of those got announced.

item.title: Google Says Its New World Model Generates Its Own Sound, and Characters That Talk Back
item.description: DeepMind's Genie 4 builds interactive worlds from a sentence and gives them voices. Its makers admit the worlds drift, and publish no safety result.

item.title: Anthropic Researchers Try Deleting a Model's Cheating Instead of Punishing It
item.description: A training method routes a model's cheating into parameters that are then deleted. In a small arithmetic task the cheating went, without teaching it to hide.

item.title: Learned to Invent Problems, Until Its Makers Changed the Reward
item.description: Training an auditor on the wrong reward produced one that invented findings. Pairwise rewards fixed it, and it improved on a hostile benchmark.

item.title: An Outside Red Team Found Ways Around OpenAI's Own Agent Monitors
item.description: METR and Redwood stress-tested OpenAI's internal misalignment monitoring and found bypasses, an unmonitored compaction gap, and a deferrable monitor.

item.title: Anthropic Tests Reveal Weaknesses in AI Coding-Agent Security Monitors
item.description: Anthropic's red team found substantial bypasses against the blocking monitors in Claude Code Auto Mode and OpenAI Codex. Controlled tests, not incident rates.
